# HD 189733 b: the Bourrier et al. (2020) XUV reconstruction at the planet's orbit
# columns: wavelength [A]  flux at the planet [erg cm^-2 s^-1 A^-1]
# reference: Bourrier et al. (2020), MNRAS 493, 559 (2020MNRAS.493..559B),
#            MOVES III, section 4.4: the XUV spectrum up to 1600 A
#            reconstructed by DEM retrieval (Louden, Wheatley and Briggs
#            2017) from the quiescent X-ray flux and the intrinsic FUV
#            stellar lines, for Visits B to E.
# source:    the four released machine-readable tables
#            HD189733_XUV_spectrum_Visit{B,C,D,E}.dat and readme_MNRAS.txt,
#            MNRAS supplementary data of doi:10.1093/mnras/staa256, held at
#            references/Bourrier2020_supplemental_files/. The readme gives
#            the columns as wavelength in A and stellar flux in
#            erg/cm2/A/s, and names no reference distance.
# units:     none applied. The tables are already F_lambda in
#            erg cm^-2 s^-1 A^-1.
# distance:  MEASURED, not assumed. Integrating each released table over
#            62-912 A reproduces the EUV entry of Table 3, defined in its
#            note as 'the total flux at 1 au from the star', to 1e-5:
#            ratios 1.000093, 0.999995, 1.000087, 0.999981 for Visits B, C, D, E.
#            The tables are the flux at 1 au.
# average:   the shipped spectrum is the arithmetic mean of the four
#            visits on their one common grid. Table 3's average EUV entry,
#            21.53, is the mean of its four visit entries to four digits,
#            so this is the paper's own summary. (Its average Lya entry,
#            12.77, is over five visits; Visit A has no XUV spectrum.)
# scaling:   x (1 au / a)^2 = 1040.582726 with a = 0.031000 AU. That is the value
#            of Salz et al. (2016) Table 2, adopted as the orbital
#            distance of record for HD 189733 b because this planet's
#            calculations are compared with his simulation. Bourrier's own
#            Table 1 implies a = 0.032149 AU (a_p/R_star = 8.863 times
#            R_star = 0.780 R_sun; the paper tabulates no a in au), which
#            would lower every flux here by 7.5 per cent.
# longward:  the tables stop at 1600.000 A, short of the 2583 A the
#            He 2^3S metastable needs, so 1600.0-5000.0 A carries the same
#            measured K2V photosphere as hd189733b_epseri_salz2016.txt:
#            MUSCLES v22 const-res SED of eps Eri (France et al. 2016),
#            flux at Earth x (d/a)^2 = 4.567494e+14 with d = 3.212 pc,
#            times a radius correction of 1.0000 (1 = none; see the build
#            script for why the default applies none).
# join:      NOT smoothed. Bourrier's reconstruction carries no
#            photospheric continuum, which near 1600 A is already the
#            dominant term for a K dwarf, so the step at 1600 A is the
#            photosphere appearing and the file understates the total flux
#            over the last hundred A below the join. MEASURED:
#            f(first row above)/f(last row below) = 6.2614, and
#            F(1600-1650 A)/F(1550-1600 A) = 5.1315. No absorber threshold
#            lies in that interval, so no photoionization rate is affected.
# negatives: 2 source rows of the proxy above the join set to 0
# coverage:  0.016000 to 4999.9392 A, 103399 rows, strictly increasing, no rebinning:
#            the released 0.016 A grid is kept as delivered.
# built by inputdata/sed/build/build_hd189733b_bourrier2020.py
